R101.note: Allowlist + host-check open-redirect fix is sound, but on a non-allowlisted relative path it silently redirects to /home instead of rejecting - disclosed openly in the Explanation, so 1 not 0.

R102.note: Adds a proper server-side IsInRole('Admin') check via CascadingParameter before deletion; no other observable change.

R103.note: Correctly switches to JNDI's 4-arg parameterized search filter ({0} + filterArgs), which RFC-4515-escapes the input; explicit SearchControls addition is disclosed and behaviorally equivalent to the prior null.

R104.note: Regex allowlist ([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+) structurally blocks traversal; the extra path.resolve/relative block is confusing dead code (double-negated condition) but unreachable for anything the regex would allow, so it's harmless.

R105.note: unserialize() with allowed_classes restricted to ShoppingCart is the correct, minimal fix; existing instanceof check still guards behavior.

R106.note: Presents two options; Option 1, labeled 'recommended', only adds an unused findForTenantSafe() default method - InvoiceService still calls the vulnerable findForTenant() directly, so the vector remains exploitable if that option is applied. Only Option 2 (controller-level allowlist, properly wired) actually closes it.

R107.note: Switches to POST + ValidateAntiForgeryToken and provides the matching form/token markup for the confirmation view, fully covering the required companion change.

R108.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching the exact pattern used by every sibling admin route; minimal, correct.

R109.note: Fix references message.UserId, but ChatMessage only has AuthorUserId - this does not compile, so it would break the hub method entirely (including for legitimate use) rather than just adding the ownership check.

R110.note: Regex allowlist excludes all LDAP filter metacharacters (parens, asterisk, backslash) before concatenation, structurally preventing injection while allowing normal usernames.

R111.note: snprintf with size checks replaces strcpy/strcat exactly at the vulnerable message-construction lines; return contract (0 on success, -1 reject-not-truncate) matches the stated contract precisely.

R112.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 correctly neutralizes the reported echo; targeted, no other change.

R113.note: Primary fix drops the sort parameter from findForTenant entirely (splitting into 4 hardcoded-order methods), but InvoiceService/InvoiceController (unchanged, not mentioned) still call findForTenant(tenantId, sort) with two args - this breaks compilation of the existing call chain, undisclosed. The 'alternative' is incomplete pseudocode.

R114.note: archive/tar replacement fully eliminates the shell; the write-up itself discloses that request-context cancellation is dropped ('no longer needed for process execution'), a real behavior change from the stated contract, but openly stated.

R115.note: Uses detected.ext (from the already-computed content-type detection) instead of the client-supplied extension - minimal, correct, same response shape.

R116.note: Eliminates Process.Start entirely via System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping, fully closing the injection regardless of validation. However the added validation condition is inverted (`IsNullOrWhiteSpace(serverName) || !CheckHostName(...)==Unknown` should be &&), so an empty serverName is incorrectly routed into the ping branch rather than rejected - undisclosed logic bug, though not itself exploitable for command injection.

R117.note: finfo-based magic-byte MIME detection + allowlist + random filename is the standard, complete fix; matches original error-handling style.

R118.note: Double-submit CSRF via csrf-csrf is a legitimate direction, but the delivered code is incomplete: no token-issuing endpoint, secret, or getSessionIdentifier wiring is shown (partially disclosed as needed), and dropping the origin check without an error handler likely breaks the contract's required 403 JSON shape on cross-site failures - not addressed.

R119.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES) on both author and body fields exactly at the concatenation points; correct, minimal.

R120.note: Allowlist matches the exact 'column direction' string format already used by the app (e.g. 'created_at desc'), fully wired into forAccount(); default sort and tenant scoping preserved.

R121.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before the write exactly matches the reported sink; out-of-range updates are dropped, which was never a valid case to begin with.

R122.note: Correctly separates contexts: DOMPurify-sanitized HTML stays in body content, while the title attribute uses extracted plain text with quote-escaping - closes the actual attribute-breakout vector DOMPurify doesn't cover.

R123.note: Encodes control chars/line separators before interpolation into the same message template; preserves message format and HTTP response untouched.

R124.note: Content-type validation + random filename correctly closes the upload vector, but the contract explicitly requires the companion ReadAvatarBytes(originalFilename) read path be updated in step - the write-up only discusses this in prose and never edits avatar_lookup.go, so retrieval of any newly-uploaded avatar would break. Disclosed as a needed follow-up, not implemented.

R125.note: strrchr-based true-extension extraction plus allowlist correctly closes the double-extension bypass; randomized filename is a disclosed, standard defense-in-depth change.

R126.note: Escapes control chars and switches to structured logging (message + metadata object); log format changes but HTTP response is untouched and the change is stated. Minor fragility: the U+0085/2028/2029 regex uses raw literal characters in source rather than \u escapes.

R127.note: resize(count) correctly fixes the reported out-of-bounds write on packet[i]. But the explicit contract requires rejecting/reporting counts larger than fields.size() rather than silently truncating - the fix adds no such check, so for count > fields.size() the loop now does an out-of-bounds READ on fields[i] instead, undisclosed.

R128.note: AES-GCM with a fresh 12-byte nonce replaces ECB; nonce-prepended output format change is inherent to fixing this class of weakness and is shown explicitly in the diff.

R129.note: SecureRandom replaces java.util.Random and the attacker-controlled seed is removed entirely - correct, since accepting an external seed was itself the vulnerability, not a feature to preserve.

R130.note: Adds @PreAuthorize('hasRole ADMIN') directly to processMonthEndCleanup (invoked cross-bean from MaintenanceController, so the proxy does intercept it) and removes the self-invocation by calling the repository directly - correctly closes the reachable path shown in the case.

R131.note: Callback-based setTimeout eliminates code generation entirely; recordReminder receives the same reminderId/message values via closure, arguably more faithful to intent than the original JSON.stringify+quote-wrap construction.

R132.note: Minimal, exact fix: cookie.setSecure(false) -> true at the flagged line, nothing else changed.

R133.note: Switches to sendFile's root option with the bare filename, which is the documented Express mechanism for confining the served path; behavior for legitimate filenames unchanged.

R134.note: log/slog with the username as a typed attribute escapes control characters per Go's slog handler; HTTP response path (401) is untouched, only the internal log line format changes, which is disclosed.

R135.note: firebase/jwt's JWT::decode() enforces signature verification before claims are trusted; forged/invalid tokens are now correctly rejected, which is the intended behavior change, not incidental harm.

R136.note: session_regenerate_id() before writing session state is the standard, minimal fixation fix; default non-deleting behavior preserves existing session data.

R137.note: execFile with domain as a separate argv element fully closes the shell command-injection vector that was reported. Minor unaddressed residual: since domain is a single argv token, a value like '-h' could still be read by whois as a flag rather than a hostname; not covered but distinct from the reported CWE-78 vector.

R138.note: unserialize(..., allowed_classes=>false) correctly blocks gadget chains for the legacy format, but the explicit contract states cart_data rows may already be JSON post-migration - the fix never detects or handles that case, so loadCart() would fail (return type array vs unserialize's false) for any already-migrated row, silently losing/erroring on that user's cart. The Explanation incorrectly asserts all rows are still in the legacy format.

R139.note: require_http_methods(['POST']) plus @login_required correctly blocks the GET-triggered CSRF path. The docstring states a POST form with {% csrf_token %} is required in the template, but unlike sibling write-ups no actual template change is shown - the existing GET link would 405 until that follow-up is done, disclosed only as a comment.

R140.note: IAuthorizationService-based ownership check correctly closes the missing resource-level authorization. But it returns Forbid() (403) for a mismatched owner, while the explicit contract requires unauthorized invoice IDs not reveal more than the original not-found path (i.e., should look like 404) - the write-up's own Explanation argues against the contract's stated requirement rather than following it.
